newsitem.title: FRANCE: French budget likely to raise excise duties.
newsitem.headline: French budget likely to raise excise duties.

text.p: The French government is expected to raise excise duties in its 1997 budget, government sources said on Thursday.
Officials declined comment on the nature or size of these increases before the presentation later on Thursday by Prime Minister Alain Juppe of tax reform plans.

But officials have suggested in the past that any increase in excise duties over and above the rate of inflation could focus on areas that presented a risk to public health -- in other words alcohol and tobacco -- rather than on petrol duties.
One source said duties on petrol were likely to be increased in line with the rate of inflation, a raise made every year when the duty, expressed in francs, is recalculated.

Government officials have declined comment on whether the differential between different types of petrol duties, on lead-free, super and diesel will be adjusted, although a government report in May recommended these be reconsidered.

Duties on alcohol may be raised by more than the rate of inflation, since these duties, expressed in francs per unit, have not been recalculated since 1993. With these duties, the government could make up the lost ground in one increase or increase the taxes even further.
However, officials have declined comment on press reports alcohol duties will be increased.
Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure said on Wednesday duties on tobacco would rise.
France raises some 200 billion francs a year in excise duties, including 120 billion from petrol taxes and 50 billion on tobacco duties.
An increase even limited to the inflation rate, just below two percent, could raise some four billion francs.
